messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for ORCA-DED-POOL-3 — reserved-capacity-throttle (severity: P1). visible latency spike > 99th percentile and request errors from tenant OrcaHealth. pd_incident=PD-90421

pagerduty-bot: Page sent to schedule: eng-oncall (policy: reserved-pool-crit). escalation level 1.

Maya (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Starting triage — looking at the reserved pool metrics and queue.

Ben (sre): seeing sustained enqueue depth on pool ORCA-DED-POOL-3: queue_length ~ 4200 (normal <500). cpu on gpu-nodes ~ 78% but mem and GPU util under typical. latency p95 jumped from 85ms -> 3.9s. errors = 5xx_token_failures ~ 0.9%

Maya (oncall): thanks. Can you run quick KV cache evictions metric? `curl -s http://metrics.internal/tenants/orca/pool/3 | jq .kvcache.evictions_last_5m`

Ben (sre): ran it, returns "evictions_last_5m": 1240. kv cache thrashing for sure. Also seeing `batch_size` dropping; many tiny batches -> overhead.

Carla (infra): node autoscaler didn't kick because pool was pinned to reserved instances. There's no spare capacity in this reserved pool, per contract with customer. We can enable burst capacity but that needs approval (billing + safety).

Maya (oncall): escalated to Raj (eng-reliability) via @here. Need mitigation plan: short-term customer protection (reduce errors) + longer-term capacity fix.

Raj (eng-reliability): looking. Two quick mitigations: 1) route a small % (10-20%) of ORCA traffic to fallback model variant (quantized lower-cost shard) to drain queue and reduce KV pressure; 2) enable soft-throttle to shed background low-priority requests from the tenant. Which one do we want first?

Maya (oncall): do both. Start with routing 15% to fallback, and enable soft-throttle at 10rps per token for non-critical routes. Ben/Carla — can you implement?

Ben (sre): applying route override now. Command: `redwoodctl route set --tenant orca --pool ORCA-DED-POOL-3 --percent 15 --model orca-v1-fallback`

automations-bot: route change accepted. New routing rule created: ORCA -> 15% -> orca-v1-fallback. config_id=rt-7741

Carla (infra): enabling soft-throttle policy for priority < 50 for ORCA. Command: `redwoodctl policy soft-throttle apply --tenant orca --pool 3 --max-rps 10 --priority-threshold 50`

automations-bot: soft-throttle policy applied. policy_id=st-332

Ben (sre): queue_length dropping: 4200 -> 1800 in last 90s. p95 latency down to 1.4s, errors to 0.2%. KV evictions per 5m fell to 340. Good signal.

Maya (oncall): nice. Notify CS to prepare customer note, include impact and actions. Zoe?

Zoe (cs): I'll draft a short status for OrcaHealth: "We detected transient increased latency and request errors affecting your dedicated pool. We implemented temporary routing to a compatible fallback model and soft-throttling for background requests; these steps have reduced error rates. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary." Want me to send now or wait for more stabilization?

Maya (oncall): send an interim update now. Mark status: degraded -> partial mitigation.

Zoe (cs): Sent via email and the customer status page. Reference PD ID PD-90421 and include expected follow-up timeline: 2 hours for full rollback plan.

Raj (eng-reliability): root cause note for later: sustained tiny-batch traffic from Orca feature flag rollout + heavy KV cache churn combined with reserved pool saturation. Fallback model has smaller KV footprint and better quantized memory usage.

Ben (sre): I'm patching pool autoscale policy to allow 2-instance burst for emergency only; will require finance approval for billing. Command preview: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool ORCA-DED-POOL-3 --burst-instances 2 --ttl 10m` (not applying until approval).

Carla (infra): I've manually drained a problematic worker pod that had OOM-adj behaviour; `kubectl delete pod worker-orca-17 -n ded-orca` — new pod spun up, joined pool. That reduced one noisy-victim.

Maya (oncall): system checks look good. p95 700-900ms now, queue ~520. Keep monitoring for next 15m. If stable, we can close PD.

pagerduty-bot: PD-90421 acknowledged by Maya. Incident status: acknowledged -> investigating.

(5m later) Ben (sre): still stable, p95 ~680ms, errors ~0.08%. No regression in fallback route. Queue steady ~430.

Maya (oncall): ok plan: keep routing 15% to fallback for 1 hour, keep soft-throttle in place, and follow up with a post-incident with RCA and recommended capacity change or feature-flag rollback. Raj to own RCA, Ben to own short-term capacity formal request, Zoe to follow-up with OrcaHealth. I'm going to handoff to night oncall in 20m; leaving clear runbook.

Maya (oncall): Handoff: next oncall is Ben. If anything flares above p95 2s or errors >0.5%, escalate to oncall-lead and open PD to level 2.

Ben (sre): Ack handoff. I'll monitor and escalate if needed.

automations-bot: PD-90421 status updated: monitoring -> mitigation in-place.

Maya (oncall): Closing thread here since mitigation successful and owner assigned. I will add the timeline to the incident tracker and link logs.

Ben (sre): adding logs snippet to incident tracker: `grep "orca" /var/log/redwood/requests.log | tail -n 200` saved to /incidents/PD-90421/logs.txt

Raj (eng-reliability): I'll draft RCA doc and recommended change: increase reserved burst to 2 or add auto-eviction tuning. ETA: 24h.

Zoe (cs): Customer updated again with closure note. They saw degraded UX for ~7 minutes, thanked us for swift mitigation.

incident-bot: Incident PD-90421 marked resolved by Maya. Resolution reason: overflow mitigated via fallback routing and soft-throttle; queued requests drained; monitoring stable for 30m.

Maya (oncall): Thanks team. Follow-up tasks assigned in Asana: PD-90421-RCA, billing-approval-burst, pool-autoscale-tune.

Ben (sre): thumbs up :thumbsup:

Carla (infra): good catch. leaving a note to revisit reserved-capacity SLAs: don't want silent saturation again.

Raj (eng-reliability): will include traffic pattern suggestions to the docs.
